definitions.explanation: The front part or surface of a building, object, or person. Often refers to the main entrance side of a structure.
Used adverbially with から to mean confronting something directly without evasion. Implies facing an issue or challenge straightforwardly.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}の{正面|しょうめん}に{入|い}り{口|ぐち}がある。
examples.english: The entrance is at the front of the building.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{正面|しょうめん}に{大|おお}きな{広場|ひろば}がある。
examples.english: There is a large plaza in front of the station.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}は{正面|しょうめん}から{撮|と}ったほうがいい。
examples.english: It would be better to take this photo from the front.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}に{正面|しょうめん}から{向|む}き{合|あ}う。
{彼|かれ}は{批判|ひはん}を{正面|しょうめん}から{受|う}け{止|と}めた。
{困難|こんなん}な{課題|かだい}に{正面|しょうめん}から{取|と}り{組|く}む{姿勢|しせい}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to have the attitude of tackling difficult challenges head-on.

notes:
USAGE:
As a noun, {正面|しょうめん} refers to the front side of something. With the particle から, it forms the adverbial expression {正面|しょうめん}から, meaning "head-on" or "directly." This adverbial use is very common and carries a nuance of not avoiding or evading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正面|しょうめん}{玄関|げんかん}: front entrance
- {正面|しょうめん}{口|ぐち}: front gate/entrance
- {正面|しょうめん}から{向|む}き{合|あ}う: to face head-on
- {正面|しょうめん}{衝突|しょうとつ}: head-on collision

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {前面|ぜんめん}: front surface (more physical/spatial, less figurative)
- {表|おもて}: front side, surface (everyday word for "front" of flat objects)
